title: Cell Structure and Organisation
seo_title: Secondary 3 Biology: Cell Structure and Organisation Worksheets (O-Level 6093 with Answers)
standard_code: O-Level Biology (6093): Cell Structure and Organisation
standard_text: Identify the cell structures of typical plant and animal cells as seen under a light microscope and an electron microscope, including the cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, vacuoles, chloroplasts, mitochondria, ribosomes, rough and smooth endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi body, and state their functions; relate the structure of specialised cells to their functions; describe the levels of organisation (cells, tissues, organs and systems); calculate magnification and actual size (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Biology 6093 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 O-Level Biology worksheets on cell structure and organisation: plant and animal cells, organelles, specialised cells, levels of organisation and magnification. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Plant cells add a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole.
body_html:
How to think about it

Every part of a cell has a job.

  • Nucleus: DNA and control. Mitochondria: aerobic respiration. Ribosomes: proteins. Rough ER: carries ribosomes. Smooth ER: lipids. Golgi body: packages proteins.
  • Plant cells also have a cellulose cell wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole with cell sap.
  • Specialised cells are adapted: root hair cells (large surface area), red blood cells (no nucleus, biconcave), muscle cells (many mitochondria).
  • Magnification = image size ÷ actual size, with both in the same unit.
Example

Image 12 mm, actual 40 µm. Magnification?

12 mm = 12 000 µm

12 000 ÷ 40

Answer: ×300

Example

Why many mitochondria in sperm?

mitochondria release energy

energy to swim

Answer: energy for movement

Common mistakes

  • Saying animal cells have a cell wall.
  • Mixing up ribosomes (proteins) and smooth ER (lipids).
  • Dividing actual size by image size.
  • Forgetting to change mm to µm before dividing.

faq.q: What is the difference between rough and smooth endoplasmic reticulum?
faq.a: Rough ER has ribosomes on it and transports the proteins they make. Smooth ER has no ribosomes and makes lipids and breaks down harmful substances.
Magnification = image size ÷ actual size. Change both lengths to the same unit first (1 mm = 1000 µm).
